segments.name: first-fetch

inset.label: ON THE DIE: CORE → RING → DMI

say: The reset is over. One thread, on one core, starts out in 16-bit real mode, just like an 8086 from 1978.
The reset is over. One thread, on one core, starts out in sixteen-bit real mode, just like an eighty eighty-six from nineteen seventy-eight.
Its first instruction sits sixteen bytes below 4 GiB.
Its first instruction sits sixteen bytes below four gigabytes.
There's no RAM yet, and the caches are off. So the fetch leaves the die, crosses to the chipset, and is read out of the flash chip that holds the firmware.
